verses.zh: 亚当的后代记在下面。（当　神造人的日子，是照着自己的样式造的，
verses.en: This is the record[NOTE:1] of the family line[NOTE:2] of Adam.When God created humankind,[NOTE:3] he made them[NOTE:4] in the likeness of God.
notes: Heb “book” or “roll.” Cf. NIV “written account”; NRSV “list.”
Heb “generations.” See the note on the phrase “this is the account of” in 2:4.
The Hebrew text has אָדָם (ʾadam).

Heb “him.” The Hebrew text uses the third masculine singular pronominal suffix on the accusative sign. The pronoun agrees grammatically with its antecedent אָדָם (ʾadam). However, the next verse makes it clear that אָדָם is collective here and refers to “humankind,” so it is preferable to translate the pronoun with the English plural.

verses.zh: 并且造男造女。在他们被造的日子，　神赐福给他们，称他们为「人」。）
verses.en: He created them male and female; when they were created, he blessed them and named them “humankind.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew word used here is אָדָם (ʾadam).

verses.zh: 亚当活到一百三十岁，生了一个儿子，形像样式和自己相似，就给他起名叫塞特。
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] Adam had lived 130 years he fathered a son in his own likeness, according to his image, and he named him Seth.
notes: Heb “and Adam lived 130 years.” In the translation the verb is subordinated to the following verb, “and he fathered,” and rendered as a temporal clause.

verses.zh: 亚当生塞特之后，又在世八百年，并且生儿养女。
verses.en: The length of time Adam lived[NOTE:1] after he became the father of Seth was 800 years; during this time he had[NOTE:2] other[NOTE:3] sons and daughters.
notes: Heb “The days of Adam.”
Heb “he fathered.”
The word “other” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 亚当共活了九百三十岁就死了。
verses.en: The entire lifetime[NOTE:1] of Adam was 930 years, and then he died.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “all the days of Adam which he lived”

The genealogy traces the line from Adam to Noah and forms a bridge between the earlier accounts and the flood story. Its constant theme of the reign of death in the human race is broken once with the account of Enoch, but the genealogy ends with hope for the future through Noah. See further G. F. Hasel, “The Genealogies of Gen. 5 and 11 and their Alleged Babylonian Background,” AUSS 16 (1978): 361-74; idem, “Genesis 5 and 11, ” Origins 7 (1980): 23-37.

verses.zh: 塞特活到一百零五岁，生了以挪士。
verses.en: When Seth had lived 105 years, he became the father of[NOTE:1] Enosh.
notes: Heb “he fathered.”

verses.zh: 塞特生以挪士之后，又活了八百零七年，并且生儿养女。
verses.en: Seth lived 807 years after he became the father of Enosh, and he had[NOTE:1] other[NOTE:2] sons and daughters.
notes: Heb “he fathered.”
Here and in vv. 10, 13, 16, 19 the word “other” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 塞特共活了九百一十二岁就死了。
verses.en: The entire lifetime of Seth was 912 years, and then he died.

verses.zh: 以挪士活到九十岁，生了该南。
verses.en: When Enosh had lived 90 years, he became the father of Kenan.

verses.zh: 以挪士生该南之后，又活了八百一十五年，并且生儿养女。
verses.en: Enosh lived 815 years after he became the father of Kenan, and he had other sons and daughters.

verses.zh: 以挪士共活了九百零五岁就死了。
verses.en: The entire lifetime of Enosh was 905 years, and then he died.

verses.zh: 该南活到七十岁，生了玛勒列。
verses.en: When Kenan had lived 70 years, he became the father of Mahalalel.

verses.zh: 该南生玛勒列之后，又活了八百四十年，并且生儿养女。
verses.en: Kenan lived 840 years after he became the father of Mahalalel, and he had other sons and daughters.

verses.zh: 该南共活了九百一十岁就死了。
verses.en: The entire lifetime of Kenan was 910 years, and then he died.

verses.zh: 玛勒列活到六十五岁，生了雅列。
verses.en: When Mahalalel had lived 65 years, he became the father of Jared.

verses.zh: 玛勒列生雅列之后，又活了八百三十年，并且生儿养女。
verses.en: Mahalalel lived 830 years after he became the father of Jared, and he had other sons and daughters.

verses.zh: 玛勒列共活了八百九十五岁就死了。
verses.en: The entire lifetime of Mahalalel was 895 years, and then he died.

verses.zh: 雅列活到一百六十二岁，生了以诺。
verses.en: When Jared had lived 162 years, he became the father of Enoch.

verses.zh: 雅列生以诺之后，又活了八百年，并且生儿养女。
verses.en: Jared lived 800 years after he became the father of Enoch, and he had other sons and daughters.

verses.zh: 雅列共活了九百六十二岁就死了。
verses.en: The entire lifetime of Jared was 962 years, and then he died.

verses.zh: 以诺活到六十五岁，生了玛土撒拉。
verses.en: When Enoch had lived 65 years, he became the father of Methuselah.

verses.zh: 以诺生玛土撒拉之后，与　神同行三百年，并且生儿养女。
verses.en: After he became the father of Methuselah, Enoch walked with God[NOTE:1] for 300 years,[NOTE:2] and he had other[NOTE:3] sons and daughters.
notes: With the seventh panel there is a digression from the pattern. Instead of simply saying that Enoch lived, the text observes that he “walked with God.” The rare expression “walked with” (the Hitpael form of the verb הָלָךְ, halakh, “to walk” collocated with the preposition אֶת, ʾet, “with”) is used in 1 Sam 25:15 to describe how David’s men maintained a cordial and cooperative relationship with Nabal’s men as they worked and lived side by side in the fields. In Gen 5:22 the phrase suggests that Enoch and God “got along.” This may imply that Enoch lived in close fellowship with God, leading a life of devotion and piety. An early Jewish tradition, preserved in 1 En. 1:9 and alluded to in Jude 14, says that Enoch preached about the coming judgment. See F. S. Parnham, “Walking with God,” EvQ 46 (1974): 117-18.
Heb “and Enoch walked with God, after he became the father of Methuselah, [for] 300 years.”
The word “other” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 以诺共活了三百六十五岁。
verses.en: The entire lifetime of Enoch was 365 years.

verses.zh: 以诺与　神同行，　神将他取去，他就不在世了。
verses.en: Enoch walked with God, and then he disappeared[NOTE:1] because God took[NOTE:2] him away.
notes: The Hebrew construction has the negative particle אֵין (ʾen, “there is not,” “there was not”) with a pronominal suffix, “he was not.” Instead of saying that Enoch died, the text says he no longer was present.

The text simply states that God took Enoch. Similar language is used of Elijah’s departure from this world (see 2 Kgs 2:10). The text implies that God overruled death for this man who walked with him.

verses.zh: 玛土撒拉活到一百八十七岁，生了拉麦。
verses.en: When Methuselah had lived 187 years, he became the father of Lamech.

verses.zh: 玛土撒拉生拉麦之后，又活了七百八十二年，并且生儿养女。
verses.en: Methuselah lived 782 years after he became the father of Lamech, and he had other[NOTE:1] sons and daughters.
notes: The word “other” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 玛土撒拉共活了九百六十九岁就死了。
verses.en: The entire lifetime of Methuselah was 969 years, and then he died.

verses.zh: 拉麦活到一百八十二岁，生了一个儿子，
verses.en: When Lamech had lived 182 years, he had a son.

verses.zh: 给他起名叫挪亚，说：「这个儿子必为我们的操作和手中的劳苦安慰我们；这操作劳苦是因为耶和华咒诅地。」
verses.en: He named him Noah,[NOTE:1] saying, “This one will bring us comfort[NOTE:2] from our labor and from the painful toil of our hands because of the ground that the Lord has cursed.”
notes: The name Noah appears to be related to the Hebrew word נוּחַ (nuakh, “to rest”). There are several wordplays on the name “Noah” in the story of the flood.

The Hebrew verb יְנַחֲמֵנוּ (yenakhamenu) is from the root נָחָם (nakham), which means “to comfort” in the Piel verbal stem. The letters נ (nun) and ח (khet) pick up the sounds in the name “Noah,” forming a paronomasia on the name. They are not from the same verbal root, and so the connection is only by sound. Lamech’s sentiment reflects the oppression of living under the curse on the ground, but also expresses the hope for relief in some way through the birth of Noah. His words proved to be ironic but prophetic. The relief would come with a new beginning after the flood. See E. G. Kraeling, “The Interpretations of the Name Noah in Genesis 5:29, ” JBL 48 (1929): 138-43.

verses.zh: 拉麦生挪亚之后，又活了五百九十五年，并且生儿养女。
verses.en: Lamech lived 595 years after he became the father of Noah, and he had other[NOTE:1] sons and daughters.
notes: The word “other” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 拉麦共活了七百七十七岁就死了。
verses.en: The entire lifetime of Lamech was 777 years, and then he died.

verses.zh: 挪亚五百岁生了闪、含、雅弗。
verses.en: After Noah was 500 years old, he[NOTE:1] became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
notes: Heb “Noah.” The pronoun (“he”) has been employed in the translation for stylistic reasons.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 5:1-2
1This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day when God created man, He made him in the likeness of God. 2He created them male and female, and He blessed them and named them Man in the day when they were created.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Genesis 5 has been described as the death chapter, but Gen. 5:21-24 holds out great hope for the
redemption of mankind in the "translation" of Enoch. The same terms are used for Elijah in 2 Kgs. 2:3,5,9,10.

- There are three ways the Bible describes how humans come into God's presence/realm:

- physical death

- translation (i.e., Enoch and Elijah)

- resuscitation: brings back physical life, but only for a period of time (i.e., Lazarus)

5:1 "the generations of" This term (BDB 410) is repeated ten times in Genesis (cf. Gen. 2:4; 5:1; 6:9; 10:1; 11:10,27;
25:12,19; 36:1; 37:2). This seems to imply a written cuneiform document (probably clay tablets). In ancient Mesopotamian cuneiform
tablets, a term or phrase was used to link several clay tablets together as a literary whole (i.e., colophon). I believe
that Moses used

- oral traditions from the Patriarchs

- written sources from the Patriarchs

- direct revelation to write the Pentateuch

This phrase often closes a context. It can function as a closing literary marker.

▣ "In the day when God created man" This may start another separate cuneiform stone tablet because it
summarizes Genesis 1-2.

▣ "He made him in the likeness of God" This is a major theological statement, alluding to Gen. 1:26-27.
Also note the "re-creation" after the flood in Gen. 9:6. Humanity (i.e., male and female, Gen. 5:2) are unique
creatures of the planet. They were created (see word study on bara at Gen. 1:1) for fellowship
(i.e., Gen. 3:8). If as John Walton asserts, this planet is YHWH's Temple, then humans are His physical image
in that Temple!

5:2 "named them man" Notice that this is the generic use of "adam" (BDB 9), as Gen. 5:3,4,5. This generic
use is another affirmation of the mutuality between men and women in Genesis 1-2.

▣ "in the day" This is the use of "day," not as a twenty-four hour period of time, but an age or period
of time. This same usage can be seen in Gen. 2:4; Ps. 90:4.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DAY (Yom)

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 5:3-5

3When Adam had lived one hundred and thirty years, he became the father of a son in his own likeness, according to his image, and named him Seth. 4Then the days of Adam after he became the father of Seth were eight hundred years, and he had other sons and daughters. 5So all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years, and he died.

5:3 "Adam . . . became the father of a son in his own likeness, according to his image" Here, "Adam" is a
proper name as in Gen. 4:24. There are two possible interpretations of this phrase:

- like other earthly animals, Adam produced offspring after his own kind (cf. Gen. 1:11)

- this shows that God's image (cf. Gen. 1:26-27) is still in mankind even after the fall

▣ "and named him Seth" Genesis 4:25-26 really should go with Genesis 5. Seth (BDB 1011, KB 1667 II)
is the new beginning of a godly line (cf. Luke 3:38). The meaning of the name "Seth" is uncertain (KB 1666-1667).
Cain's line will be completely destroyed in the flood.

5:5 "all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years" There has been much discussion about the
length of human life before and immediately after the great flood (i.e. the antediluvian period). Some have asserted that

- it is figurative

- they calculated years differently

- sin had simply not pervaded the earth as it has today

- the large numbers were used to show honor for previous leaders as in the Sumerian lists of ten ancient kings

The Sumerian kings before the flood lived much longer than the kings
after the flood, much as in the genealogies of the Bible. So these "years" may be an idiomatic way of denoting prestige
or fame. See NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 654-662, "Genealogy in the OT," pp. 654-662, for the specific discussion of the length
of their lives, p. 659.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 5:6-8
6Seth lived one hundred and five years, and became the father of Enoch. 7Then Seth lived eight hundred and seven years after he became the father of Enosh, and he had other sons and daughters. 8So all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.

This is referred to earlier in Gen. 4:26.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 5:9-11
9Enosh lived ninety years, and became the father of Kenan. 10Then Enoch lived eight hundred and fifteen years after he became the father of Kenan, and he had other sons and daughters. 11So all the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years, and he died.

5:10 "Kenan" This can mean:

- "possessor"

- "child"

- "created thing"

- "young man"

- "spear-man" (BDB 884)

It is obvious with this many options (as is so often the case) that we simply do not know its meaning (BDB 884, KB 1098).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 5:12-14
12Kenan lived seventy years, and became the father of Mahalalel. 13Then Kenan lived eight hundred and forty years after he became the father of Mahalalel, and he had other sons and daughters. 14So all the days of Kenan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died.

It is obvious that these are paralleled or standardized literary statements.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 5:15-17
15Mahalalel lived sixty-five years, and became the father of Jared. 16Then Mahalalel lived eight hundred and thirty years after he became the father of Jared, and he had other sons and daughters. 17So all the days of Mahalalel were eight hundred and ninety-five years, and he died.

5:15 "Mahalalel" This means "praise of El" or "El is shining" (BDB 239, KB 553).

▣ "Jared" This means "descending" (BDB 434, KB 435).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 5:18-20

18Jared lived one hundred and sixty-two years, and became the father of Enoch. 19Then Jared lived eight hundred years after he became the father of Enoch, and he had other sons and daughters. 20So all the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty-two years, and he died.

5:18 "Enoch" This name possibly could mean

- "beginner"

- "dedicated"

- "initiator" (BDB 335)

See note at Gen. 4:17b for similarity in the names between Cain's line (i.e., chapter 4) and Seth's line
(i.e., chapter 5).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 5:21-24
21Enoch lived sixty-five years, and became the father of Methuselah. 22Then Enoch walked with God three hundred years after he became the father of Methuselah, and he had other sons and daughters. 23So all the days of Enoch were three hundred and sixty-five years. 24Enoch walked with God; and he was not, for God took him.

5:21 "Methuselah" This could mean either (1) "man of the javelin" or (2) "man of weapons" (BDB 607), but all suggestions
of the meaning of these early names are speculation. He is said to have lived longer than any other person in the Bible
but no reason or emphasis is attached to this fact. Rabbinical Midrash says that the flood came on the day that Methuselah died.

5:22 "Enoch walked with God" This Hebrew VERB (BDB 229, KB 246, Hithpael IMPERFECT
with waw) in the Hithpael stem denotes intimate fellowship almost to the connotation of "to live with." As
with all these ancient Hebrew names, we are simply not sure of their exact meaning ("Enoch," BDB 335). Hebrews 11:5
describes Enoch's walk of faith. The only other person this phrase is used for is Noah in Gen. 6:9.

5:24 "for God took him" These same words (BDB 542, KB 534, Qal PERFECT) are used to describe
Elijah in 2 Kgs. 2:3,5,9,10. This implies translation into God's presence without facing physical death (i.e., translated, not resurrected).
Enoch's relationship with God resulted in intimate personal fellowship.

In a chapter replete with the phrase "and he died"
this is a refreshing example of hope

- of the love of God

- for all who trust in Him

For a brief discussion on the hope of a life after death, see Dictionary of Biblical Imagery,
"Afterlife," pp. 17-20 and "Immortality," pp. 568-570.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 5:25-27
25Methuselah lived one hundred and eighty-seven years, and became the father of Lamech. 26Then Methuselah lived seven hundred and eighty-two years after he became the father of Lamech, and he had other sons and daughters. 27So all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred and sixty-nine years, and he died.

5:26 "Lamech" This name possibly means:

- "strong"

- "youth"

- "warrior"

- "conqueror" (BDB 541)

KB mentions an Arabic root meaning "very powerful man." This name is also found in Cain's line
(cf. Gen. 4:18ff). This implies

- the name was common

- there is some connection between the two genealogies

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 5:28-31

28Lamech lived one hundred and eighty-two years, and became the father of a son. 29Now he called his name Noah, saying, "This one will give us rest from our work and from the toil of our hands arising from the ground which the Lord has cursed." 30Then Lamech lived five hundred and ninety-five years after he became the father of Noah, and he had other sons and daughters. 31So all the days of Lamech were seven hundred and seventy-seven years, and he died.

5:28 What a contrast are the two Lamechs. One is boastful of violent revenge (Cain's line); the other is
hopeful of the mercy of God (Seth's line)!

5:29 "Noah" This name (BDB 629) is a popular, not a philological, etymology of the term "rest" or
"resting place" (BDB 629). This seems to express Lamech's faith, that through Noah, a significant reversal
of the curse of Gen. 3:17 would take place. This is Lamech's statement of faith.

SPECIAL
TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 5:32

32Noah was five hundred years old, and Noah became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

5:32 "Shem" This term may mean "renown" or "name" (BDB 1028, KB 1551 II).

▣ "Ham" This term may mean "to be hot" or "to be dark" (BDB 325, KB 325 III).

▣ "Japheth" This term may mean "beauty" or "spreading" (BDB 834, KB 424).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What is the theological relationship between Genesis 4 and 5?

- Why is the genealogy of Cain developed and then totally dropped from Scripture?

- Why are the names of the Cainites and the Sethites so similar?

- What happened to Enoch?
